memory_candidates.content: When a shell helper resolves an 'extensions root' that can live OUTSIDE the calling script's own REPO_ROOT (e.g. via a .claude-extensions.json source_dir indirection to an external source-store repo), every downstream `git -C "$REPO_ROOT" ls-files <path-under-the-resolved-root>` call and REPO_ROOT-relative path-stripping computation must be re-targeted at the RESOLVED root's own git worktree, not REPO_ROOT's -- `git -C` with a pathspec outside its own repo silently resolves zero files rather than erroring, so a resolver fix alone can leave every downstream consumer reporting false 'declared but absent' findings. Fix pattern: derive a second variable (e.g. EXT_GIT_ROOT) via `git -C "$EXT_DIR" rev-parse --show-toplevel`, falling back to REPO_ROOT when EXT_DIR is not itself inside a git worktree (preserves every existing caller's behavior exactly), and route every git/path computation in the affected loop through it instead of REPO_ROOT.

common_test_resolve_subject's mode vocabulary (deployed / source-store / deploy-tree-first) has no 'source-store-first-with-deployed-fallback' order -- only the opposite-direction deploy-tree-first, or single-mode-only deployed/source-store. A test suite that genuinely needs source-store-preferred-with-deployed-fallback (matching the convention that a suite validating a fresh source-store edit must not silently test a stale deployed copy) cannot express that via common_test_resolve_subject and should stay on common_test_resolve_candidate with an explicit two-candidate list in [source-store, deployed] order -- then add a permanent, individually-reasoned exemption to lint-subject-resolution-declaration.sh's EXCLUDED_FILES array (it naively flags any common_test_resolve_candidate call against a literal '.claude/scripts' candidate as an 'unmigrated implicit-order shape') rather than forcing a semantically-wrong migration just to satisfy the lint.

verify-deploy.sh's gate 3 (doc-lint) and gate 5 (manifest-driven content-hash equality) 'Content differs from source' / 'deployed script content drift' findings are DEPLOY-FRESHNESS checks (deployed .claude/ file content vs. the agent-system/extensions source file content, read directly off disk) -- they are NOT git-commit-status checks. Committing a source-store edit does nothing to clear this finding; only running an actual deploy (<leader>al / deploy-headless.sh) does, and a repo whose plan explicitly forbids initiating a deploy as a Non-Goal will see this finding persist for every source-store-only edit until the next deploy cycle, which is expected and not a regression.
